body:
We're going to keep fighting for our beliefs and what the Voting Rights Act stands for, no matter what the Supreme Court says, because we're confident that we're on the right side of history and we will prevail.
Team, fuel our efforts with $35 or more today to help activate and turn out every voter to win at the ballot box in these midterm elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=051226_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Mother Jones: Blame John Roberts for Destroying the Voting Rights Act [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=051226_3&amount=25]
Team: Louisiana v. Callais is based on a lie . It also represents the culmination of John Roberts' decades-long mission to end the Voting Rights Act.
First, the lie: Writing for the majority in the Supreme Court's decision gutting the Voting Rights Act, Justice Alito declared that " the racial gap in voter registration and turnout has largely disappeared ." That's simply not true, and Trump's Department of Justice has admitted to the press, after the fact, that it used alternative measures to write the report that Alito cited.
In truth, amongst underrepresented communities in comparison to their peers:
➜ 2020 voter turnout was 14% lower.
➜ 2022 voter turnout was 23% lower.
➜ 2024 voter turnout was 17% lower.
These numbers represent actual people – predominantly voters of color, young people, and women – whose voices are being systematically pushed out of our elections. The gap Justice Alito says has "largely disappeared" is real, ongoing, and growing.
Team: In the wake of the Supreme Court’s ruling, we’re redoubling our efforts to ensure every eligible American has a voice in our democracy, but we need your support. Will you chip in $35 right now? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=051226_3&amount=35]
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=051226_3&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=051226_3&amount=25]

GIVE $250 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=051226_3&amount=250] Other Amount [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=051226_3&amount=35]
As for John Roberts? He's written or joined the majority on every major case the VRA has faced -- 2013's Shelby County v. Holder , 2021's Brnovich v. DNC , and now 2026's Louisiana v. Callais .
His self-appointed mission to end the Voting Rights Act started in the 1980s , when he was just a young lawyer working in Ronald Reagan's Justice Department. He fought Congress on behalf of Reagan's administration, essentially claiming the VRA was affirmative action for voting rights. A bipartisan Congress in the 1980's disagreed, overwhelmingly reauthorizing the VRA and strengthening it over Roberts' objections.
Fast forward to his confirmation hearings for Chief Justice, when we called the VRA a "settled question," then, upon being confirmed, immediately got to work ending it . He wrote the majority opinion for Shelby County v. Holder , knocking the first leg out from under the VRA and setting the stage for a decade-plus of further challenges.
Striking down the last remnants of the Voting Rights Act is exactly why the Roberts Court held this case over from last year. He's accomplished his mission to take us backwards in time and allow racial gerrymandering to be a standard practice, silencing more voters. The VRA no longer stands in the way of white majorities locking racial minorities out of elected office through race-based gerrymandering.
This is the fight of our lives, Team, and we need you with us. Pitch in $35 or however much you can to help us fulfill the mission of the VRA by informing and turning out every voter possible for the upcoming elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=051226_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
https://www.facebook.com/voteraction [https://www.facebook.com/voteraction] https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org [https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org] https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/ [https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/] https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/ [https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/]
Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.
Your support is crucial to our efforts. Will you donate today to help us protect voting rights? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=051226_3&amount=20]

But despite the millions being spent by my opponents, **we are still in the thick of this fight** because of grassroots supporters like you.
Now we enter the final week.

If we’re going to keep our ads on the air, reach undecided voters, and finish strong, **I need your help right now.**

body:
And a new office in Madison!
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260512-2807)
Peter,
Yesterday, we celebrated the grand opening of Team Hong's first campaign office in Madison. This is a space for volunteers and supporters to connect, build community and organize to get Fran elected.
Also: If you've been wanting a yard sign, this is your sign to stop by! We have them available for a suggested donation of $10.
**Address:** 1342 Dewey Ct, Madison
**Hours:** Monday & Tuesday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260512.mhGuAu&refcode=em20260512-2807&t=1&akid=2807%2E105371%2Ew6ymkH)
Our office will also serve as a mutual aid hub! We're collecting nonperishable food and personal care items, **with drop-off hours on Monday and Tuesday afternoons from 2 to 5 p.m.**
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260512.mhGuAu&refcode=em20260512-2807&t=2&akid=2807%2E105371%2Ew6ymkH)
We're entering a serious phase of the primary — AKA, the part where we start spending the serious money it takes to run a statewide campaign. Rent for an office is a big line item, but it's nothing compared to what media and mailers cost.
We know every dollar is precious right now. Trump's war with Iran has gas over $4.40 a gallon and grocery prices climbing.
So many of you have given so generously already, and we're deeply grateful. But now is the time to put even more energy behind Fran — she has gone from wildcard candidate to genuine frontrunner.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260512.mhGuAu&refcode=em20260512-2807&t=3&akid=2807%2E105371%2Ew6ymkH)
**[The primary is just 91 days away. Chip in $5, $10, $100 — whatever you can — and help us make better possible.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260512.mhGuAu&refcode=em20260512-2807&t=4&akid=2807%2E105371%2Ew6ymkH)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260512.mhGuAu&amount=5&refcode=em20260512-2807&t=23&akid=2807%2E105371%2Ew6ymkH)**
See you in Madison!
— Team Hong
**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_fh_footer?refcode=em20260512-2807&t=24&refcode2=2807_105371_w6ymkH&akid=2807%2E105371%2Ew6ymkH)**

Email us: [info@francescahong.com](mailto:info@francescahong.com)
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is one of the most powerful tools that grassroots campaigns like ours have to reach everyday people across Wisconsin and beyond, so thank you for reading to the end.
The more people who engage with our emails, the more likely we’ll go straight to your inbox. For a free and easy way to help our campaign, please [click this link to our website](https://francescahong.com/) after you finish reading our emails.

Over the past year, we’ve built an incredible grassroots movement. We’ve traveled to every corner of this state. We broke fundraising records. And against all odds – we took a narrow lead in the polls.
**But then, my billionaire opponent began unloading his massive warchest against us. He wrote his own campaign a check for $25 million. He poured $10 MILLION into ads to soften his extreme image and to spread ugly, baseless attacks against me.**

Narrative:
On 05-12-2026, I responded to a disturbance at Team Rogers HQ regarding a missed fundraising goal.

Upon arrival, I found the team visibly shaken. Staffers stated that despite our best efforts, we were going to fall short of our fundraising goal.

body:

============================================================

Good afternoon!

We’re excited to invite you to the Grand Opening Celebration of the newly improved San Bruno Mountain Day Use Area!

Join San Mateo County Parks, California State Parks, and community members as we celebrate exciting new improvements that make this beautiful outdoor space more welcoming and accessible for everyone.

📅 Wednesday, May 13, 2026
⏰ 11:00 AM
📍 Saddle Area – San Bruno Mountain
555 Guadalupe Canyon Parkway, Brisbane, CA

The improvements include:
✅ ADA-accessible picnic areas
✅ Brand-new restroom facility
✅ Interpretive pavilion & displays
✅ Scenic mountain views
✅ Family-friendly outdoor gathering space

Enjoy a fun community ribbon-cutting celebration, photo opportunities, and the chance to explore one of our county’s most scenic outdoor destinations.

Bring a picnic, enjoy the fresh air, and celebrate this exciting park improvement project with us!

We hope to see you there. Please RSVP to Mike: ** mrichardson@smcgov.org (mailto:mrichardson@smcgov.org?subject=May%2013th%20Event%20)

David J. Canepa

**The $2.1 Million Retirement Problem**
---
_ **Most Americans have 7 cents of every dollar they'll need to retire. And rising costs are spending what's left.** _
---
Here's the number: **$2.1 million. **

That's what the average American says they need to retire comfortably -- according to a 2025 national survey by BlackRock.

Larry Fink -- BlackRock's CEO and the man managing more retirement money than anyone else on earth -- put it bluntly in his annual letter:

"Almost no one is close."

Now add what Fidelity just projected.

The average couple will face **$345,000 in healthcare costs alone** during retirement -- enough to buy a house in most parts of America. That doesn't include a single mortgage payment, grocery bill, or utility.

And that's the conservative number. It excludes long-term care entirely. Factor that in, and newer research puts the real number closer to **$400,000.**

Take a look at your own 401(k)...

[Can it carry you through 20 or 30 years of rising expenses...](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4NzV9AAwAAAAAAJqzBHAEk5J6gyVGuUrbaeM0z-kyCTckaScwht5sskHNCgslw5xf6vi_qNWbSh3YK-dqyyfaY1cJXaetiAesPAO6rfyNVax1zLufRSDuQg "20 or 30 years of rising expenses...") plus a medical bill that could rival a second mortgage?

Here's what most people don't realize until it's too late:

Your 401(k) and IRA are paper assets. They're tied to a stock market that swings wildly and a dollar that loses purchasing power every single year.

You used to be promised a retirement. Now you're just hoping for one.

Last year, a record percentage of Americans dipped into their 401(k)s just to cover emergency expenses. Many aren't saving for retirement anymore -- **they're surviving on it. **

Millions are heading into retirement dangerously underprepared. Most won't realize it until the window to act has already closed.

**But you still have time.**

What retirement actually requires now is an asset that sits outside the traditional paper system -- one that can help diversify risk when markets are volatile.

When the market and dollar weaken, it preserves your wealth. It carries no counterparty risk, answers to no central bank, and has outlasted every financial crisis in history.

That asset is **physical gold.**

And the data backs it up.

While 401(k)s bled value through 2025 and into 2026, gold surged past $5,000 an ounce -- hitting a **record high of nearly $5,600** in early 2026. And in 2025, gold was up more than 55% in a single year.

Most Americans never hear about what comes next -- because the financial industry profits from keeping your money exactly where it is.

**Federal tax law gives you the right to move your existing 401(k) or IRA directly into physical gold -- held in a gold IRA -- without triggering taxes or penalties. **

It's legal. It's IRS-approved. And it's available right now.

**The $2.1 Million Retirement Problem**
---
_ **Most Americans have 7 cents of every dollar they'll need to retire. And rising costs are spending what's left.** _
---
Here's the number: **$2.1 million. **

That's what the average American says they need to retire comfortably -- according to a 2025 national survey by BlackRock.

Larry Fink -- BlackRock's CEO and the man managing more retirement money than anyone else on earth -- put it bluntly in his annual letter:

"Almost no one is close."

Now add what Fidelity just projected.

The average couple will face **$345,000 in healthcare costs alone** during retirement -- enough to buy a house in most parts of America. That doesn't include a single mortgage payment, grocery bill, or utility.

And that's the conservative number. It excludes long-term care entirely. Factor that in, and newer research puts the real number closer to **$400,000.**

Take a look at your own 401(k)...

[Can it carry you through 20 or 30 years of rising expenses...](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4NzV9AAwAAAAAAJvkW4Cf-D2ZwzhldgGc0BIOVgCuOtVPvPIr-iZ7AqmJocRU6oP229lSB0YycCr-RKlhzZ9tPpl4bdeCEGBsm3SbgCmrRglBo2Au8gIiZw "20 or 30 years of rising expenses...") plus a medical bill that could rival a second mortgage?

Here's what most people don't realize until it's too late:

Your 401(k) and IRA are paper assets. They're tied to a stock market that swings wildly and a dollar that loses purchasing power every single year.

You used to be promised a retirement. Now you're just hoping for one.

Last year, a record percentage of Americans dipped into their 401(k)s just to cover emergency expenses. Many aren't saving for retirement anymore -- **they're surviving on it. **

Millions are heading into retirement dangerously underprepared. Most won't realize it until the window to act has already closed.

**But you still have time.**

What retirement actually requires now is an asset that sits outside the traditional paper system -- one that can help diversify risk when markets are volatile.

When the market and dollar weaken, it preserves your wealth. It carries no counterparty risk, answers to no central bank, and has outlasted every financial crisis in history.

That asset is **physical gold.**

And the data backs it up.

While 401(k)s bled value through 2025 and into 2026, gold surged past $5,000 an ounce -- hitting a **record high of nearly $5,600** in early 2026. And in 2025, gold was up more than 55% in a single year.

Most Americans never hear about what comes next -- because the financial industry profits from keeping your money exactly where it is.

**Federal tax law gives you the right to move your existing 401(k) or IRA directly into physical gold -- held in a gold IRA -- without triggering taxes or penalties. **

It's legal. It's IRS-approved. And it's available right now.

## US Inflation Rate Rises to 3-Year High
U.S consumer prices rose 3.8% from a year ago, topping economists' expectations and marking [the steepest single-month surge](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OqzAURldjOpBt7AsULl5Dl9dOiRz_hDu62Mg4Qdn9iBSzgak_6Xw65-u23CwSpsd_uwVTY15SOA8KtYayYIpkK-ZU8MD0SE9HwZbjeV8kl9By3Yp-8RbpvajGmxiCDH0TjBiGEQBGwZvVuGHSoCSMcOdO9FZ50WsbndLRalBTg-aicS16wTlo3k2TEF55ABtHcNExxYPHmkv3nTHVNUR651conctbQ2atdT9Y_4_Jmcn5PM_Opbu7RibnC83kzDWTs5BMzm7H9tertXtBaj823Vo3aorx-4lEeMDAFH9sFunzU_8U52XkTwAAAP__W6N2Dw) since May 2023. Prices rose 0.6% on a monthly basis, easing from March's 0.9% pace, as the Iran war continued pushing fuel and food costs higher, new government data showed Tuesday. [See the full breakdown here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFyhCAURb8GOxxARS0o0tht2pTOEx7rSxAcZNfZv8-4RX4g9Z05d875us03oEDx_gkbmuLTHPE8ApaCeaboAxRKMdNB8R4fNiDk47HMSijNRcdlMzug8JrbyhmPqLCp0Mi-H7TWgxTVaqD1uHg9gPdNC7aHbpCuV6MeR6d6O1RkLproZCOF0J2ox1FK1zqtwQ_aestagY5KyvV3olhW9OGVnphrm7YqmLWU_WDNB1MTU9N5nrWNi71GpqYLzdQkOqYmqZia_pz4khF-XDoj9ylz2DMF_vayO3G7Qi71WrZQZeP2k0KgQ_esFfcNKLyvy796PY36DQAA__-c-X5U). Core inflation, which excludes energy and food, [came in at 2.8% annually](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGu3CAUheHV2N21AGNgCoo07l7alBYDF_tGGEaA58m7jyZFNpD-6OjX9-tr-3KUKO8_3Ym2x7Jl_G4Je8e6UY7JdSq5UqO858sndLVdz00woYAtwOctOEr3JsdgI6LAeUTLtTZKKcPZeFhhgpDPRc9SBIOLmtFEJiR65DqYBxvJft7YwmfOmFrY9HhwHmRQykWjfPSDZBiolzr9LpT7gTHd5Y118uUckz16f7Vh_jGIdRBrpOyyx-l2RymfxSBW9CWX8x7E6monn3AQqy-5XSdWeFXy2KBddccAswHK4F6VEsRaTnBwo6vg9gKh0hszPG_AjHW_4Z8PcL1o-Zi1mY5-prHa8PqmlKgpPUi2n47S39r-X8RvK_4EAAD__52IkgY) and 0.4% monthly, both above forecasts, suggesting price pressures are spreading beyond the pump. Airline fares soared 20.7% over the past year as rising jet fuel costs were passed directly to travelers, while beef prices climbed 14.8% annually.
## Pentagon Surfaces Secret Nuclear Sub
The Pentagon made a rare and deliberate disclosure Monday, [revealing the location](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DHO4yAQxfHT4M4RxmbABcU27rLtlhaBIZ7VGCIgiXL7VfYKX_2efsX_z3W_emLK99_-RNdT2TO-G2PvWHfKiX2nkis1yvf8DIy-tudtV1LBKPU4zXv0xJ99GaJLiArnAd1kjAUAO8nhcEZ7YxXMsErpV7mC9mG2CjXc5ggWB3JfTeppnqQELS_rOk1xiQA-WQgpiEVipF7q5W-h3A9M_CkvrJdQzoHd0fujifmXUJtQWz_wIObvJtT2KEzhI9QWMWFuKNSmrVFGLmM5qIyBfWvjSa0R49iet9NXyt_bUF18vImZGhixyPvp6b869B9lejn1LwAA___imHuB) of an Ohio-class nuclear-armed submarine in Gibraltar as a show of force toward Iran. Sub locations are typically classified. The Sixth Fleet [released an image](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOozAQBOCnMZ2RvYAhhYtr6HLtlWht1rB3xkS2E5S3P-Uv_hf469GMPs2f-3JHjpy233iQreFcEl0lUq2UF04hYuUzZS6ctvT0kTCXp1tAgZFqkLpbVuT4XvpmtYEIqGvI6nGcjDGTVs1uMbje37TqRjU6gJUGmLwbTND91CscG7afNTXoTitlBtXeblqv_WoMhsn44EWvaOV65vbvyanuFOL7fFFu_Xk00e61PorofgmYBczXdbWlZn5Q-eQCZpcx-Z2KgDnh6y1g_tZrATNnTHJjlzFWytJhjFwqe3lwKRxJlqc7MHMiiRHLP5SgTTeBGdu9HrHJdn1c_CmZUfRqO5Djl6z-6M6Xhf8BAAD__4ODiWQ) of the vessel docked at the British territory off Spain's southern coast. The Navy didn't officially name it, but ship watchers identified it as the USS _Alaska_ , which can carry Trident II missiles with a range exceeding 4,500 miles. The disclosure came a day after President Trump rejected Iran's latest peace offer as "totally unacceptable" and said the ceasefire was on "life support." The Pentagon is also weighing [renaming the war](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2u2zAQhE8jdTT4Z0qvYJHG3UubUliRS3kDaimQ9BN8-0C-QroBPmAw3_z5Xr6BMvH2G3b0PZWF8WwZe8e6EKcMnQpXasQbv0JGqO21LlpqJ-RdKLNEoPxe7Bh9QtRoRvRqmmbn3Kzk-PS4uqTBoJ1WtyZrZqNUnJ2cwx3dtLqR_NUm78ooKd1d3r6-lIo2OgdpdiGFwUqM1Eu9_S3E_Ykpv8sP1lso-5j9s_ejDebXoB-DfpzneeM1XBYXH_TjKJk6hTboB39sIIuG4VWpvy-M3GErLELhRhEr8SYqCob9SlSBxQlVtIxxwyfsO1YREBomqihCyRmOJmpgMNY6I8fq43FSztTcNFi57UD5s7X_18E_Xv8LAAD__x8Sk60) "Operation Sledgehammer" if the ceasefire collapses and combat resumes.
## What a Gas Tax Cut Saves by State
President Trump said Monday he'd back [suspending the 18.4-cent federal gas tax](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGupCAYBeCn0Q4DKIxTUGxjN9tuaRB-9N8gGPgd77z9jfcVbv0lJ-ecf6_5ZTFiWv_aHQyFPCe4agQiKDOmEC1hTgUrpjWdLoIt9VxmyaVmXDHRz95i_MxD600AkNC3YMTjMWqtR8HbzQglABbulFNej2rxEniQToanG2H0fYvmTuNK9IJzrXj3fArhB6-1DaN2wTUDB4-US_c_Y6INQvzkN5TO5b2NZiM6atP_aeTUyOm6ri4t7l5xeyOnI0ckdPXGDQnYls8KjZyonPvBqv1UVs_jyIVYPesByWNaWQAPxUa22srIfrHiku2HQY2qLcYfF8aIVT-aga-7xfhThn714NvI7wAAAP__GVyIUw) as the national average hit $4.50 a gallon, up more than 50% since the Iran war began. ### AI Lobby Is Already Winning
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/@theangrydem)

---
| | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9wdWIvbWF0dGRpZW1lci9wL2FudGhyb3BpYy1hbmQtdGhlLW5ldy1tb25vcG9seS1ibHVlcHJpbnQ_.m6IV0vRYnB8HTyREtuGqBDBfmbwdCALR22ohsiCm9IM?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)

| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/mattdiemer/p/anthropic-and-the-new-monopoly-blueprint?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

[Regulatory capture](https://substack.com/redirect/b08017ef-e306-42be-ac18-e3ec11822b07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is one of the oldest ways companies stop competition while pretending they are protecting the public. It is when an industry helps create the rules that govern that industry, then uses those rules to build a moat around itself. The public hears "safety." The politicians hear "responsibility." The company hears "no more competition."
And we are watching it happen right now in real time.
We are seeing it in cryptocurrency. We are seeing it in AI. And after watching the All In podcast the other day, where [David Sacks](https://substack.com/redirect/6dd20e9d-62dd-4b2d-81e6-c89e2a63150b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (Trump's A.I. Czar) basically screamed for everyone to pay attention, I think this needs to be said plainly. Because the trick here is not subtle once you understand the playbook.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/a2dada56-5e6e-4fb1-bb93-94e2792b9849?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**First** , you amplify the problem.
**Then** you present yourself as the responsible actor.
**Then** you fund the politics around the problem.
**Then** you help write the rules.
**Then** the rules just so happen to favor the companies already big enough to comply.
That is regulatory capture.
And right now, Anthropic is giving us a case study.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/fd75b377-17f3-405f-8c37-00f7132b1343?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
### Step One: Create the Fear, Then Offer the Cure
For AI companies to move into Washington and ask for regulation, there has to be a problem. And to be clear, there are real problems. People are worried about AI for legitimate reasons. They are worried about jobs, water use, electricity use, data centers, farmland, privacy, deepfakes, national security, and whether these companies are building something society cannot control.
Those concerns are not fake. People are right to be concerned.
But this is where the manipulation starts. A company can take real public concern, amplify it, wrap itself in responsibility, and then show up in Washington saying, "Please regulate us before something terrible happens."
That sounds altruistic. It sounds like an industry is **finally** taking responsibility.
But...
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/765439f5-aed5-4714-a30b-7661330aa8e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Dario Amodei](https://substack.com/redirect/e8e97944-7575-4e0e-8892-1376c8054afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Dario Amodei](https://substack.com/redirect/e8e97944-7575-4e0e-8892-1376c8054afe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the CEO of Anthropic, has become one of the loudest AI doom voices in the industry. He has warned about massive white-collar job losses. He has talked about unemployment spikes. He has warned about AI writing most code. He has raised concerns about civilization-level threats, biological weapons, autonomous weapons, deception, blackmail, and systems that may operate beyond human control.
When the CEO of one of the biggest AI companies spends a lot of time warning the public that AI could be dangerous, and then that same ecosystem starts moving money into politics to shape AI regulation, you should at least stop and ask what the hell is going on.
Because the message is very convenient.
AI is dangerous.
We are the responsible ones.
The government must act.
We are here to help write the solution.
That is the first step.
* * *
### Step Two: Build the Political Machine
Once the fear is established, the next step is political money.
Enter the Jobs and Democracy PAC, funded by Anthropic. According to the information I am working from, Anthropic put $20 million into this PAC, and the **[PAC recently spent almost $500,000](https://substack.com/redirect/6deca949-feb8-47d5-a054-78d3ce1c19c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on TV ads supporting [Brian Poindexter](https://substack.com/redirect/718b712c-2e2b-4346-9869-ed7613fef457?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in his congressional primary. [But a total of $1.3 million in total spend from Jan 1, 2026 (as far as we know). ](https://substack.com/redirect/89fedaf5-2401-4c51-bbd1-11ef896f670c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/528ab96d-48d4-436b-807f-d181ed582ea4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Now, let 's talk about what a Super PAC does.**
Anthropic knows exactly what a Super PAC is. They know it can spend unlimited money promoting candidates. They know this is considered political speech. They also know Super PACs cannot legally coordinate with campaigns.
**And that is not just a bug in the system. That is also a very convenient feature.**
Because it gives everyone plausible deniability.
The campaign can say, "We cannot control what outside groups do." The candidate can say, "We are not coordinating with them." The PAC can say it is independent. The company can say it is supporting "responsible regulation." And the voters are supposed to pretend all of these walls are made of steel instead of paper.
The second layer is even more important. This is not just any corporate-funded PAC. This is a PAC that can present itself as being for democracy, jobs, and responsible AI regulation. So when people raise concerns about corporate money, the response becomes, "Well, isn't this good? Don't we want AI regulated? Don't we want responsible technology?"
And that is exactly the trap.
Because the regulation being demanded is already being framed by the same industry that benefits from it.
* * *
### Step Three: Write the Rules Before Anyone Else Understands the Game
Most members of Congress do not understand AI. They do not understand crypto either. They do not understand the technical systems, the market dynamics, the open-source implications, the infrastructure requirements, or the long-term competitive consequences.
That is not even necessarily an insult. These are massive, complicated fields, and Congress deals with everything from agriculture to defense to health care to tax law to foreign policy. Nobody knows everything.
So what happens?
Lobbyists show up.
"Experts" show up.
PAC-funded influence networks show up.
Industry-backed nonprofits show up.
Lobbyists buy million-dollar townhouses in Washington, host events, build relationships, circulate white papers, draft model legislation, and slowly become the people lawmakers rely on to understand the issue.
Then when the time comes to regulate AI, who already has the framework written?
**The companies! (lobbyists)**
Some lawmakers will listen to Anthropic. Some will listen to OpenAI. Some will listen to Google. Some will listen to xAI. Some will listen to whoever has the best relationships, the best lobbyists, the best events, or the most money moving around the political system.
And then the rules start to take shape.
On the surface, they will sound reasonable. They always do. Testing requirements. Licensing. Know-your-customer systems. Safety reviews. Registration. Reporting. Compliance departments. Liability rules. Security audits.
Again, I am not saying every one of those ideas is bad.
But ask who can afford them.
Who can hire the lawyers? Who has the congressional friends? Who can build the compliance teams? Who can survive years of regulatory process? Who can meet complicated federal requirements? Who can lobby for technical language that looks neutral but just happens to crush open-source competitors and smaller startups?
The biggest companies can.
That is the moat.
* * *
### The Rockefeller Lesson
This is why the David Sacks analogy on All In was so useful. He laid out a thought experiment about John D. Rockefeller and Standard Oil. Rockefeller was one of the most ruthless monopolists in American history, but Sacks makes the point that Rockefeller was terrible at public relations.
So imagine if he had been better at it.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/99e8741c-1cfa-4532-8628-d1c5781ad1fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Imagine if Rockefeller had not called his company Standard Oil. Imagine he called it Safe Oil. Imagine he went around warning everyone that kerosene was dangerous. Which, of course, it was. It could light your house, burn it down, torch a city, or be used to make a bomb.
Then imagine Rockefeller calling for a government agency to regulate kerosene safety. Testing. Licensing. Common-sense standards. Rules for wick thickness. Rules against dangerous independent refiners. A whole debate over what makes oil safe.
People would have gotten lost in the debate over safety while missing the real move. Rockefeller would have been building the richest, most powerful monopoly in history under the moral cover of protecting the public.
That **is** the point.
A company can be right about danger and still be using that danger to eliminate competition.
That is what people need to understand.
* * *
### Competition Is the Threat They Actually Fear
Companies do not like competition. Big companies especially do not like open-source competition. Digital companies do not like open ecosystems when closed ecosystems make more money. They want users trapped inside their products, their models, their platforms, their APIs, their pricing structures, and their rules.
Open-source AI is a threat to that. Smaller startups are a threat to that. Independent developers are a threat to that. Competitive markets are a threat to that.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/9a268668-537b-43b8-a097-4904927ecfa1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
So if you are a massive AI company, what is the best way to stop them?
You do not say, "Please ban our competitors because we would like to become a monopoly." That would be too obvious.
You say, "This technology is dangerous, and we need serious safety rules."
Then you help define the rules.
Then those rules require compliance systems that only a few companies can afford.
Then the small companies die. The open-source models get squeezed. The independents get buried under red tape. And the largest companies carve up the industry as they see fit.
That is regulatory capture.
And that is why David Sacks, (**remember, he is the Czar of AI & Crypto for the Trump administration**) was warning that if Anthropic continues on its current trajectory, it could become one of the most powerful monopolies ever created. He also pointed directly at anti-competitive behavior.
* * *
### The Political Trick
**This is why I keep coming back to the money in these races.**
A lot of people hear that a corporate-backed PAC supports AI regulation and think, "Well, that sounds good." They hear that the PAC cannot coordinate with the candidate and think, "Well, then it is separate." They hear that the company is worried about AI safety and think, "Well, maybe they are being responsible."
But that is how the whole structure works.
The company amplifies the fear.
The company funds the political vehicle.
The political vehicle supports candidates.
The candidates can deny coordination.
The PAC can claim moral purpose.
The public gets told the whole thing is about safety.
Then the industry helps write the regulations that determine who survives.
That is not **fucking** benign. That is not some innocent little civic engagement project. That is a complete **fucking** manipulation.
And yes, people will say, "But we need regulation."
Fine. I agree.
But regulation written by whom? For whose benefit? With whose money? With whose lobbyists in the room? With which competitors excluded? With which open-source projects crushed? With which candidates supported along the way?
Those are the questions.
* * *
### This Is How Power Works
[](https://substack.com/redirect/8d989f35-deeb-4bda-8f8f-c2cc9215ff43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The entire point of this is not that AI should be unregulated. The point is that we need to understand how regulation can be used as a weapon.
If we are not careful, we are going to wake up in a world where a handful of AI companies wrote the rules for everyone else, crushed open competition, trapped users inside closed systems, and then told us they did it all for our own safety.
Create the problem, or amplify it.
Present yourself as the responsible adult.
Fund the politics.
Write the rules.
Kill the competition.
Call it safety.
That is why this matters. And that is why we **cannot** just shrug and say, "Well, they support regulation, so it must be fine."
Because sometimes the most dangerous power grab does not come from the company saying regulation is bad.
Sometimes it comes from the company saying, "Please regulate us."

When the CEO of one of the biggest AI companies spends a lot of time warning the public that AI could be dangerous, and then that same ecosystem starts moving money into politics to shape AI regulation, you should at least stop and ask what the hell is going on. Because the message is very convenient. AI is dangerous. We are the responsible ones. The government must act. We are here to help write the solution. That is the first step. Step Two: Build the Political Machine Once the fear is established, the next step is political money. Enter the Jobs and Democracy PAC, funded by Anthropic. According to the information I am working from, Anthropic put $20 million into this PAC, and the on TV ads supporting in his congressional primary. | | ---|---|--- Now, let 's talk about what a Super PAC does. Anthropic knows exactly what a Super PAC is. They know it can spend unlimited money promoting candidates. They know this is considered political speech. They also know Super PACs cannot legally coordinate with campaigns. And that is not just a bug in the system. That is also a very convenient feature. Because it gives everyone plausible deniability. The campaign can say, "We cannot control what outside groups do." The candidate can say, "We are not coordinating with them." The PAC can say it is independent. The company can say it is supporting "responsible regulation." And the voters are supposed to pretend all of these walls are made of steel instead of paper. The second layer is even more important. This is not just any corporate-funded PAC. This is a PAC that can present itself as being for democracy, jobs, and responsible AI regulation. So when people raise concerns about corporate money, the response becomes, "Well, isn't this good? Don't we want AI regulated? Don't we want responsible technology?" And that is exactly the trap. Because the regulation being demanded is already being framed by the same industry that benefits from it. Step Three: Write the Rules Before Anyone Else Understands the Game Most members of Congress do not understand AI. They do not understand crypto either. They do not understand the technical systems, the market dynamics, the open-source implications, the infrastructure requirements, or the long-term competitive consequences. That is not even necessarily an insult. These are massive, complicated fields, and Congress deals with everything from agriculture to defense to health care to tax law to foreign policy. Nobody knows everything. So what happens? Lobbyists show up. "Experts" show up. PAC-funded influence networks show up. Industry-backed nonprofits show up. Lobbyists buy million-dollar townhouses in Washington, host events, build relationships, circulate white papers, draft model legislation, and slowly become the people lawmakers rely on to understand the issue. Then when the time comes to regulate AI, who already has the framework written? The companies! (lobbyists) Some lawmakers will listen to Anthropic. Some will listen to OpenAI. Some will listen to Google. Some will listen to xAI. Some will listen to whoever has the best relationships, the best lobbyists, the best events, or the most money moving around the political system. And then the rules start to take shape. On the surface, they will sound reasonable. They always do. Testing requirements. Licensing. Know-your-customer systems. Safety reviews. Registration. Reporting. Compliance departments. Liability rules. Security audits. Again, I am not saying every one of those ideas is bad. But ask who can afford them. Who can hire the lawyers? Who has the congressional friends? Who can build the compliance teams? Who can survive years of regulatory process? Who can meet complicated federal requirements? Who can lobby for technical language that looks neutral but just happens to crush open-source competitors and smaller startups? The biggest companies can. That is the moat. The Rockefeller Lesson This is why the David Sacks analogy on All In was so useful. He laid out a thought experiment about John D. Rockefeller and Standard Oil. Rockefeller was one of the most ruthless monopolists in American history, but Sacks makes the point that Rockefeller was terrible at public relations. So imagine if he had been better at it. Imagine if Rockefeller had not called his company Standard Oil. Imagine he called it Safe Oil. Imagine he went around warning everyone that kerosene was dangerous. Which, of course, it was. It could light your house, burn it down, torch a city, or be used to make a bomb. Then imagine Rockefeller calling for a government agency to regulate kerosene safety. Testing. Licensing. Common-sense standards. Rules for wick thickness. Rules against dangerous independent refiners. A whole debate over what makes oil safe. People would have gotten lost in the debate over safety while missing the real move. Rockefeller would have been building the richest, most powerful monopoly in history under the moral cover of protecting the public. That is the point. A company can be right about danger and still be using that danger to eliminate competition. That is what people need to understand. Competition Is the Threat They Actually Fear Companies do not like competition. Big companies especially do not like open-source competition. Digital companies do not like open ecosystems when closed ecosystems make more money. They want users trapped inside their products, their models, their platforms, their APIs, their pricing structures, and their rules. Open-source AI is a threat to that. Smaller startups are a threat to that. Independent developers are a threat to that. Competitive markets are a threat to that. So if you are a massive AI company, what is the best way to stop them? You do not say, "Please ban our competitors because we would like to become a monopoly." That would be too obvious. You say, "This technology is dangerous, and we need serious safety rules." Then you help define the rules. Then those rules require compliance systems that only a few companies can afford. Then the small companies die. The open-source models get squeezed. The independents get buried under red tape. And the largest companies carve up the industry as they see fit. That is regulatory capture. And that is why David Sacks, (remember, he is the Czar of AI & Crypto for the Trump administration) was warning that if Anthropic continues on its current trajectory, it could become one of the most powerful monopolies ever created. He also pointed directly at anti-competitive behavior. The Political Trick This is why I keep coming back to the money in these races. A lot of people hear that a corporate-backed PAC supports AI regulation and think, "Well, that sounds good." They hear that the PAC cannot coordinate with the candidate and think, "Well, then it is separate." They hear that the company is worried about AI safety and think, "Well, maybe they are being responsible." But that is how the whole structure works. The company amplifies the fear. The company funds the political vehicle. The political vehicle supports candidates. The candidates can deny coordination. The PAC can claim moral purpose. The public gets told the whole thing is about safety. Then the industry helps write the regulations that determine who survives. That is not fucking benign. That is not some innocent little civic engagement project. That is a complete fucking manipulation. And yes, people will say, "But we need regulation." Fine. I agree. But regulation written by whom? For whose benefit? With whose money? With whose lobbyists in the room? With which competitors excluded? With which open-source projects crushed? With which candidates supported along the way? Those are the questions. This Is How Power Works The entire point of this is not that AI should be unregulated. The point is that we need to understand how regulation can be used as a weapon. If we are not careful, we are going to wake up in a world where a handful of AI companies wrote the rules for everyone else, crushed open competition, trapped users inside closed systems, and then told us they did it all for our own safety. Create the problem, or amplify it. Present yourself as the responsible adult. Fund the politics. Write the rules. Kill the competition. Call it safety. That is why this matters. And that is why we cannot just shrug and say, "Well, they support regulation, so it must be fine." Because sometimes the most dangerous power grab does not come from the company saying regulation is bad. Sometimes it comes from the company saying, "Please regulate us." Stay Angry Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS by support Matt's work. Subscribe and Share! | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Matt Diemer Berea, Ohio ? ?

body:
Plus, sign up to volunteer in the final stretch
| | | | |
---
| We're now less than a week away from Election Day, and the momentum behind our campaign is stronger than ever. But these final days are critical, and we need your help reminding voters what's at stake and encouraging them to head to the polls.
I'll jump right to it - there's three items in this email:
1. Opportunities to volunteer in the final stretch
2. Invitation to Tuesday's Victory Party
3. Reminder of Early Voting

---
|
---
Volunteer
There are two important opportunities this week to help us finish strong:
Help us prepare campaign signs for delivery across the district as we head into the final stretch of this race. These signs will be used for Election Day.
Saturday, May 17th
9:00 AM
Meet at: 595 Waddell Street, Athens, GA
On Election Day itself, we need supporters to help us wave signs, greet voters, and keep our campaign's momentum visible at high-traffic locations throughout the day. This is a fun way for kids to be involved on Election Day, too!
Tuesday, May 19th
Election Day Shifts 7:00 AM - 9:00 AM 11:00 AM - 1:00 PM 4:00 PM - 7:00 PM To sign up for either opportunity, please contact Olen Anderson ASAP at 912-486-5179 or [olen@houstongaines.com](mailto:olen@houstongaines.com)
---
|
---
Election Night Celebration
Once the polls close, we hope you'll join us on Election Night as we watch the results come in and celebrate all the hard work that has gone into this campaign. If you plan to attend, YOU MUST RSVP ahead of time so our team can prepare for everyone joining us. Click below to do so.
---

---
| | [REGISTER FOR ELECTION NIGHT PARTY](https://a89bm49ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001tM0UZRR4ozgVtXZkwi2LAqOG7G9tryEs-J_NElDfBZnhopmcoXe1IzniAH7lP7iVWpjGNoCqSo8cJIoKOZ_MMvUXQq3Q30SWPTN9-d9winU3SeHBVJ9V4ISH4EgkkMc8U5QTGLL2arr6MVdW8ds9DGWbZER6jhyQcZ2ZrnqsBW4=&c=fJGesDZpGdGy7_YVAr9LbY7xdYV8mQFo-Vl5XnbyxUu0rWgSc5TZyg==&ch=hhxOcU5mVW1Rno3PCCwoigGZ7JzVy4ALQESXkEh-IrgB0DIOOj0uDw==)
---
|
---
| Early Voting Reminder
Finally, and most importantly, we are down to the final three days of early voting. Friday is the last day to vote early. Through the first two and half weeks of early voting, only 8.3% of Georgia voters have cast a ballot. At stake in this election are our Supreme Court and Court of Appeals Judges. When you vote, be sure to go all the way down the ballot--judicial races are after the party ballot questions. The left is trying to politicize our courts and put liberal activists on the bench. Don't let it happen--vote for our Supreme Court and Court of Appeals incumbent judges.
Beat the lines and get to the polls this week. When you do, it helps our campaign focus on those who haven't voted yet. To find your early voting location and see a sample ballot, [click here](https://a89bm49ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001tM0UZRR4ozgVtXZkwi2LAqOG7G9tryEs-J_NElDfBZnhopmcoXe1I9B30S-P5jHKEQ-RfdaG8BHHve1JqFw2GQzM5HGZFumFQ8mrIqJSDgyGvZFFG8YQYG87c-Wcu9DWzn2HM-63FizohwWj53yHjHj921Zv4jH-&c=fJGesDZpGdGy7_YVAr9LbY7xdYV8mQFo-Vl5XnbyxUu0rWgSc5TZyg==&ch=hhxOcU5mVW1Rno3PCCwoigGZ7JzVy4ALQESXkEh-IrgB0DIOOj0uDw==).
---
| |

| Thank you for standing with us during these final days. Together, we'll finish strong and bring home victory on Tuesday!
Houston

Peter,
On Friday Virginia's MAGA-packed state Supreme Court overruled the results of their redistricting referendum where millions of voters went to the polls and voted for new maps to counter Trump's nationwide redistricting push.
In response, VA dems are now floating the idea of lowering the retirement age for justices so that they can appoint a new justice(s) before the midterms. Time will tell if Democrats are able to pull off this unorthodox but critically important maneuver.
Regardless, our precarious and potentially forlorn bind in Virginia serves a reminder of just how important these often overlooked State Supreme Courts really are.
Now, in just one week we have an opportunity to learn from this lesson and rob MAGA of two seats in the critical GA Supreme Court election where, as of yesterday, Democrats are now favored to win:

Sir, I am a 70 year old Black man and I know what it means to be called “Boy.”
| | | | | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001bc74j-d3UFfZ7s_bhswsePGEBRIU7qrXpfb6cWTA-sfYLN9A7-azKnIGYIHYhrAWv9weDhjKxhPkQp2OOblyqY9b5H8CZQrpStcDzB4ng7xT1Kded7LH3xOL6IsEyJxUJsakNsBdlgaOUcvOsMFpNdqPehIlplj6WPLl6A-i0xn8kK1mSdYK9_UvPZIAGB4WczoRyRIGplJ-crDi4dMsDMRAT1b0JKuD&c=mmi4WXhlfYRIe3rB9WfzB9H2nl98eUl8nVhroBOaXSu6XIijX4a4Xg==&ch=_o8qyIkdy6LwbmSD-Sgcr0Jx_LZyjiNsksHTFaOkTr8hcaPJ0njZUg==)

| Peter,
On Friday morning over 600 hundred Louisianans showed up to the Louisiana state capitol to protest and speak out against a new Congressional map proposed by the Louisiana GOP that will erase Louisiana's two black majority districts and establish all white districts.
During the hearing on redistricting, GOP State Senator Jay Morris yelled "Shut up, boy" to my Executive Director Dadrius Lanus, a Black man, who, in Sen. Morris's words was "commenting and talking" too loudly for him to concentrate.
Sir, I am a 70 year old Black man and we know what it means to be called "Boy."
---
| | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001bc74j-d3UFfZ7s_bhswsePGEBRIU7qrXpfb6cWTA-sfYLN9A7-azKnIGYIHYhrAWv9weDhjKxhPkQp2OOblyqY9b5H8CZQrpStcDzB4ng7xT1Kded7LH3xOL6IsEyJxUJsakNsBdlgaOUcvOsMFpNdqPehIlplj6WPLl6A-i0xn8kK1mSdYK9_UvPZIAGB4WczoRyRIGplKYNEH95gavX1HTVhcofn_F&c=mmi4WXhlfYRIe3rB9WfzB9H2nl98eUl8nVhroBOaXSu6XIijX4a4Xg==&ch=_o8qyIkdy6LwbmSD-Sgcr0Jx_LZyjiNsksHTFaOkTr8hcaPJ0njZUg==)
---
Senator Morris says we misheard. That the audio proves it. That he said "you all need to shut up" to the Black constituents behind him outraged that their votes won't be counted.
Senator Morris, an elected member of our legislature, thinks if he had yelled "you all need to shut up" it would be better.
It wouldn't.
What Senator Morris doesn't understand is that White people have been telling Black folk to "shut up" for over 250 years.
What Senator Morris doesn't understand is that we remember being told we were 3/5ths of a person. That even when we won personhood in the eyes of the law, they instituted poll taxes and "reading" tests. That when we marched and dreamed and cried and buried loved ones who had hung as strange fruit from tall trees because they raised their voices too loud that what Black people have always wanted is equality.
Or maybe Senator Morris does understand all that.
I don't know.
What I do know is that I am a 70 year old Black man. And I don't let anyone call me or my brothers "Boy."
[Please, chip in even $1 today. Let's show Senator Morris that they might have gutted the Voting Rights Act and canceled our election. But we shall not be silenced.](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001bc74j-d3UFfZ7s_bhswsePGEBRIU7qrXpfb6cWTA-sfYLN9A7-azKnIGYIHYhrAWXlLEI1Kjmdtjr65psNHCj3SVoh-LJ3XHkPl_agimYankCmXj6y0S0-1jg209-VcovDqdUyxBl7lALaJm3oh7L3KUkHFIHLh7Fzn9aUAPw9BrTGc1G3JRFTwGWnY6dkWas8GN2XciUK3uxMmquLs1w58y0rv0zXtczvN5vGZAX-Y=&c=mmi4WXhlfYRIe3rB9WfzB9H2nl98eUl8nVhroBOaXSu6XIijX4a4Xg==&ch=_o8qyIkdy6LwbmSD-Sgcr0Jx_LZyjiNsksHTFaOkTr8hcaPJ0njZUg==)

During the hearing on redistricting, GOP State Senator Jay Morris yelled "Shut up, boy" to my Executive Director Dadrius Lanus, a Black man, who, in Sen. Morris's words was "commenting and talking" too loudly for him to concentrate. Sir, I am a 70 year old Black man and we know what it means to be called "Boy." | | == Senator Morris says we misheard. That the audio proves it. That he said "you all need to shut up" to the Black constituents behind him outraged that their votes won't be counted. Senator Morris, an elected member of our legislature, thinks if he had yelled "you all need to shut up" it would be better. It wouldn't. What Senator Morris doesn't understand is that White people have been telling Black folk to "shut up" for over 250 years. What Senator Morris doesn't understand is that we remember being told we were 3/5ths of a person. That even when we won personhood in the eyes of the law, they instituted poll taxes and "reading" tests. That when we marched and dreamed and cried and buried loved ones who had hung as strange fruit from tall trees because they raised their voices too loud that what Black people have always wanted is equality. Or maybe Senator Morris does understand all that. I don't know. What I do know is that I am a 70 year old Black man. A report from Austin-based think tank Texas 2036 shows the state's public school enrollment dropped by more than 76,000 students from the 2024-25 school year to the current one. The 1.4% decline is the first observed since the COVID-19 pandemic and only the second since the state started tracking enrollment nearly 40 years ago.

## Public School Enrollment Down 76,000
A report from Austin-based think tank Texas 2036 shows the state's public school enrollment [dropped](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OnTAQhZ_GdEb-BwoXaeg2bUpk7GGxYmxkz17uffuIKyV5gO1m5khH832_PpYPF1PMnz_dARafW1kyXC0BItQFci0pHZAx1HK2wfyOGaE2XAQThjJNuVyCi-m1qC7YlYWJd2D5MIxmYNzIbreBGy0cN45rA9OwGi-MVIPfJqm9GlUX7V3GNJecM6FEP0oVTNCTlqNZNd-IYhAiltrjDghP17b0Kg-ovS9Hl-yOeDYifxAxEzFf19V_tRvijomY75GIeYWGtKFDuLd3DRGzqxh9ep_-IYm_OT2_1hQ9bX4vJTXaAOgWa0OaS6anywGO6Ol_S_TWRGOmAbwL0Lpqw3nFlGIzA1Hs83Axvb_G77l-WPEnAAD__43dlF4) by more than 76,000 students from the 2024-25 school year to the current one. The 1.4% decline is the first observed since the COVID-19 pandemic and only the second since the state started tracking enrollment nearly 40 years ago. The [report](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL9u8yAUR58Gb7HgYmMyMHzD5y0dqkrthhxzSVAxILjNn7evkkp9ge4__Y7OeT_YwxJiSKeXZUNDN59twmuLSITVYqo5xg0TuZpLm9RnSIS1kQUOasfHnZDWLSHe7dA5c-RuLzo0Ypq0mrhQsjubZVDiKPyqV7GfxnUVoFEr57VD9IPQXTCPMz4KKQSHAXotB6fcuB-lVsdReDZwdIFy7emMhLel-XjPF6z9mrcumjNRaUz-YzAzmJ8D4FL1uZ4YzNeyW3MiTMRg_ioxL64xmB9MBjMfGcxvH1LZ_7-u9hVLrj-OfXG-q8aVa4gxNDWxgZ-2JcQnm_5W7GLgOwAA__8znX4z) attributed the reduction to declining birth rates, shifting migration patterns, and increased competition from private schools and homeschooling. The organization projected that 100,000 fewer students could be enrolled in Texas public schools five years from now, even as the state continues to grow. Students in kindergarten through fifth grade [accounted for](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL_SmzAQxJ8GOjHS6Q98hYo0dF_alIyMDqPJIXmki7HfPoObPEC6LXZ39re_vpfvkCjl-89woOfXVpaMZyNkxrpgroXowMyxlkcb3e-UGWvjBSQ4Ia1Qeokh0XsxffQ3Gb9Uj16N4-RGqZzudz-tUQVrNTiwYDanAYIKEK0xkxxX2yd_lUmrtFISDAyTNtFF-2X15G5WbZ2RGBOXOvCOjK_QNnqXJ9ZhLUdPfmd-tE7_6GDuYD7Pc9jKawx_Gqd8WTqYL6YO5k9YtHUvhcQ_ONEQm2i4lhwFhXrHxmJPjUtNq7jQxRaImrghlVNYYcWRiFLJffXxcV66ubEz8n6ERJ9Z_H9nPj38DQAA__9pFIsi) 60% of the decline, while Hispanics accounted for 81%. Meanwhile, enrollment in urban districts has fallen by 17.3% over the last 10 years, while it has grown by 13.4% in rural districts. The report emphasized that its findings do not reflect the [impact](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uhDAQhU9jOiP_YaBwkYZu06ZEBg-LtcZG9gR2bx-xipQDpP1G8_Te93Ubb9YHH--fdgODzyWNEc4SABHyCDGnEDaI6HLaS6sfPiLkgqNgQlPWUC5HZ314japyZmKu5xUY3radbhnXslpNqwDAaaknpXvRK7d0U9t33FrhJtn1lTdXGGu45JwJJepOKqdd0zey01PDF6IYOI8p17gCwtOWJbzSAbme01YFsyLuhcgPIgYihvM868fTxutIxHCtIWJ4v9E9BY9-vkCGPWWkv_x7Cn6mZV5TCoWu9gAabL5DQRpTpHM6vKN_Nuilg_pIM8wpO3B09QVTfhExVNm4_fQh-KJboth9sz68m-L__B5G_AQAAP__NTaTQQ) of state-funded Texas Education Freedom Accounts, which were recently awarded to nearly 100,000 students. The $1 billion school choice program received more than 274,000 applications, suggesting it could expand in the future.
## Red Oak City Council Paves Way for Data Center
Red Oak's city council voted 4-1 to [rezone](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAUhJ8GOiP_GwoXt6HLbbdEhnNIrBiM7LMhefsV-wrbTTGa0fd93aZbiCnu9_9hQ0_vNU87njUhEZYJ95JT2nAnKPmozj7jTlgqTZJLy7hhQk0QYvpMugU_cxhEi14411vHhVXtw0thnRmUsKjWGaTAHhxCMPMgV6s1b6O_xrgRSggutex6pcGCGYzq7WzE2miOECmXjh5I-A51TZ_8wtIteWuTfxAdtVH_Gjk2cjzPs1vzW18YV6GR4xUbORYElsOTQaDAFrxI2BLpw5b8vS8xsaNkwkpt8XCcMaVYrWs0v28hpt8v-puhl5c_AQAA__-BYnt4) 830 acres of agricultural land for a proposed data center on Monday, despite vocal opposition from more than 130 residents. Last month, the city's planning and zoning board voted 3-2 against recommending the rezoning. More than 20 people spoke during the city council meeting's public comment period, all of whom [opposed](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGupCAYBeCnwQ4DqKgFxTZ2s-2WBv1_lAyCgX_Hmfv0N95XuPVJTs53_j3mh_XBx-2vPdDQ26U54lUCEmGeMeYUwoGRIKez9PrpI2EuNCuhNBcdl80M1ofP3FZgFgGjrNDIvh90L6Ruqt2Ada1dls7h6vQg-8UNo0NwDsZmtONaeXOXiU42UgrVqnpoWtDQjV0z6KWTjrUCwVPKNe1I-LbFhU96Ya7XdFTB7ERnYc0fpiampuu66ris4K47Zmq6PUxNIa02MDVlBJ7sk2csHjBS4ef_svPFrk9uN-tjIZ7xK0UfNw6WLF_xRjM1tUKpoRNMTVU2cF4-BF90z1qxHdaHnzn0uxNfRn0HAAD__32oh9M) the move. "_We are not opposed to data centers. We're opposed to the city putting them in our neighborhoods_ ," [said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDvOozAUhVcDndH1mxQupqHLtFMix74JVgxG9p0Qdj9itvB3RzrSeXx_7vPdp5y212-_oqPvs8wbHi0jEdYZt1pyXnGjWMverHmnjbA2mgUIw0AzLufoUz5n1Uf3gHjjPTpu7WgscCP7xYEBkF5EG5QN0YdR8eDtqPUNrNHi0Sd3hYHmknMQSgyjVNFEfdNyNA_Nn50CjIlKHWhBwq9vz3yWD9YhlLXPbiHaWyd_dWLqxHQcx3D6pZTL7cR03enE5CulkPGSFSMr_s1CopOF8ncLKTO_77V8sLFrLwAINSy05r66uB8p59SM7RS8Vp_y_176Ga2PE_8CAAD__3UIfcY) Red Oak resident Cindi Stephenson. | Peter,
Hope your spring is off to a great start!
On Thursday, June 4th, Governor Charlie Baker will join the Massachusetts Republican Party for the annual Lincoln-Reagan Reception, and I hope you can make it!
The Lincoln-Reagan Reception is a longstanding tradition in Massachusetts and plays a critical role in supporting candidates up and down the ballot.
This year, our focus is clear: regaining the corner office, supporting the hardworking candidates who carry our message in communities across the Commonwealth, and coming together with a renewed sense of unity and purpose.
The work ahead will take all of us. Events like this help ensure our candidates have the resources they need to compete and win.
I sincerely hope you'll be able to join the tradition with Governor Baker on Thursday, June 4th, at 6:00 PM at the Mandarin Oriental in Boston.
To contribute and RSVP, please use the button below or email [haley@massgop.com](mailto:haley@massgop.com) if you're ready to join the host committee.
I look forward to seeing you there!

"If you can choose one thing, choose growth." \- Dan Gilbert
I recently sat down for lunch with an elected official here in New York City. He asked me, "How is it raising a family and running a company in the City?" He was fishing for information on what business founders and parents are experiencing and what the city could be doing better.
"It's fine," I answered. "Most of my team is based here in New York and I'm not going anywhere." He seemed a little bit relieved at my answer.
For me, it was an easy choice to start Noble Mobile in New York because, well, I live here already and so did my co-founders. My kids are in schools that they enjoy, in grades 8 and 4, and you try not to have your kids switch schools unless there's a very compelling reason. Are my rent and taxes and cost-of-living higher than normal? Sure. But I'm in building mode and this is a fine place to build. I'm at a point where my choices revolve as much around my personal preferences or family priorities as optimizing for the last dollar.
There are a lot of advantages to building a company in New York. You have access to talented engineers and hires. You can establish a cohesive company culture that's industrious and creative. It's easy to meet with brands, celebrities, agencies, investors, media outlets and corporate partners. I go on CNBC or CNN or Fox or some other news network every week or so and it's a short ride to a studio. Even podcasters are more likely to be either based in New York or visit.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fc6c2c91-d428-48cc-8c04-2da913ebef60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The downsides of starting a company in New York City are primarily costs: everything is very expensive. This includes taxes, rent, employee compensation, food, healthcare, cleaning, you name it. Whatever a normal company might budget for, say, a company lunch, you can add 30 - 50% to it. We are based in the Garment District, which is highly convenient for travelers but kind of a no-frills neighborhood, partially to save money on rent.
We employ some young people at Noble Mobile. I think a lot about some recent college graduate arriving in New York the way I did back in 1996. (I graduated from college 30 years ago and am going to my reunion next week!) I was a random twenty-something-year-old wannabe entrepreneur trying to make something of myself. My rent was $1,080 to split an apartment with a friend. I walked or took the subway everywhere - a cab was an emergency measure. I would bring a book to read on the subway. I was in New York to try to access opportunities and meet people; I was the idealistic young hire who took a paycut at a small company hoping to achieve something. My parents lived in the suburbs, so I could take the train home for a nice meal during a weekend or holiday, but they moved away when I was in my mid-twenties.
The opportunities were both professional and personal; New York City had a great dating scene for twenty-somethings. I would go out late at night to an acquaintance's birthday party in the hopes of meeting someone and having sparks fly, and even if the night ended in disappointment, the late-night subway ride home felt like the end of a quest that would start again the following day or weekend. During my twenties, I moonlighted as a part-time tutor and nightclub promoter while working at various start-ups.
For me, my big break came when the little education company I tutored at needed a new CEO in 2005. I became the CEO a year later, the same year I met Evelyn. When that company was acquired 4 years later, I became a millionaire. I paid off my law school loans and all of my youthful misadventures were wiped clean. I was 34 at the time, and married Evelyn two years later.
I would never have had this kind of journey any place other than New York. It was a pressure cooker that took me from a failed entrepreneur to a guy with three jobs to eventually a successful CEO in the space of 12 years.
I'm not sure if the New York equation still works as well for young people. There's evidence that it doesn't. My tiny bedroom in that apartment would cost $2,600 today as opposed to the $1,080 I spent in 2000. There aren't as many growth opportunities where your compensation goes up at a rate that exceeds your cost-of-living. A lot of people live here for a few years and then depart because they can't afford it. The fact that I'm still in the city as a middle-aged Dad is a mild shock, as I used to regard surviving here as a victory in itself. I pay for things that I never would have imagined when I was younger, like parking and food delivery and dry cleaning. Most of the people I came up with in my twenties have long since left New York City, if only to New Jersey or Long Island or Connecticut to raise a family.
I talk to business leaders and hear that big companies are starting to shrink their footprints in the city in favor of places like Texas and Florida. New York and California are right now the states experiencing the most out-migration; that is, people are departing mainly because they're too expensive:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/76454c21-d246-4424-bc49-bf429ae2d17b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Would I tell a young person today to move to the City for their twenties out of school? Of course it's not for everyone - no place is. It's a deeply individual decision, and people will do what's inside of them. I would say it's a great place for the sense of energy and to experience a special time of one's life. If you're fortunate, you can become a bit like Liam Neeson in Taken, and develop 'a special set of skills' that might serve you well wherever you go. But I would also say that the New York of the late 90s and early 2000s I came into my own in has gotten pricier and less welcoming. It'd be good to set a clear sense of goals and a timeline for yourself, because, like a lot of the country, it's gotten tougher over time for the folks showing up here with a dream.
For a limited time only you can get **6 months** off your mobile bill with [Noble Mobile](https://substack.com/redirect/9f1b0344-19ad-43d6-92f9-d04f633f3ea0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), an absolutely crazy value that will save the average family $1,000. You read that right. Email [matt@noblemobile.com](https://substack.com/redirect/f0bd9191-ecf7-49fe-96e8-affd7be9a97a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and use my name to switch or explore. Offline no-phones party [returns](https://substack.com/redirect/5c832137-5212-4e38-ba41-ad745a63f5c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to NYC on May 21st! I'm going from that party to my college reunion. Look up.

name: Team Freedom Va
subject: Let's Celebrate!
body:
Paid Family & Medical Leave is law in Virginia
| | |
---
| |
---
| Freedom Virginia Celebrates the Signing of Paid Family and Medical Leave Legislation
---
| Friends-
This Monday, we celebrated the signing of Paid Family & Medical Leave legislation as Virginia became the first state in the South to guarantee paid leave.
---
| |
---
| Featured in the photo are Rhena Hicks, Freedom Virginia Co-Executive Director, and Chrischa Ives, Freedom Virginia storyteller, to the left of Senator Jennifer Boysko
---
| | [Read More](https://dpxqxvhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001JTwVzvGD9hAXXJJUBijFERqyfYXlz-wX1TzgcnOZZBK_Hj5f45ukBTc6rZ7DsadGYfOm1cVoTfpVRU6RHVe4uK0485GJP10ZG7E54am6L-sJbz5VOqq15ExGX_6_Zl_hL7CStgVmaRyTyUHc8Wb94B_oAVJiad_okTE4QW79l_y10KdWsBYfU167HD6ngXUpHpXT_xXosaJ68IAiI3DssXuux3xCXYoYG0OlbX1pUO0=&c=_4B7A34BuVy51zqcnf3YEM7YT2KEszOgWz2IBdph1o61Wo9-OHI8_Q==&ch=9EacI50X2iVkFWPiX8EubJwrfbr1dbPB4EYnxNFRIaJBHW9btIapqA==)
---
"Every parent- every family- knows just how valuable time is when a loved one is ill or experiences an emergency, and unfortunately, anyone who is or has been a caregiver to a chronically ill relative has likely taken a significant financial hit in order to do so. I'll never forget the first time- nor the last time- my daughter asked me, 'Can you please stay with me one more day?' and I had to tell her no. The signing of this bill ensures that so many families like mine won't have to make the heartbreaking choice between one more day with their loved one and paying for necessities. Here's to all the families who no longer have to hear the echo of a plea for 'one more day.' On behalf of Gabrielle Elizabeth Aldea, we thank you." -Chrischa Ives, advocate from Virginia Beach
We're grateful that no Virginian will ever have to choose again between caring for themselves or their loved ones and going to work to ensure they have a paycheck.
---
---

Peter,

At the end of this message, **[I’m going to ask you to make your first donation to my campaign for U.S. Senate in North Carolina.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/11161?t=8&akid=1379%2E124072%2EIsb-2Y)** But first, will you let me explain why your support – especially ahead of our mid-month deadline – is so important?
Frankly, running for Senate wasn't part of the plan. I wanted to serve North Carolina from right here at home.

Seeing all of the chaos coming out of Washington DC, I knew I had to do something. Folks had placed their trust in me throughout my career as a public servant to fight for them – and **I felt that responsibility deeply.**
This is a race I simply could not walk away from. It’s also one I know we can win.

Since launching our campaign, tens of thousands of people have joined our grassroots movement. I’m so grateful to count you as one of them, Peter.

Your contribution of $5 will be put to work immediately to help us win in North Carolina and take back the Senate. Fellow American, If this highly decorated NYPD officer had used his service weapon, I probably wouldn’t be sending you this message... ...but because Sgt. Erik Duran chose non-lethal force to stop a fleeing criminal, he’s staring down nine years behind bars. _Side-by-side with the violent criminals he helped put away during his exemplary 15-year career in law enforcement._ **[That’s why I’m urgently rallying pro-police patriots like you to help Erik fight back.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** You see, in August 2023, NYPD Sgt. Erik Duran was part of an undercover narcotics “buy-and-bust” operation in the Bronx. An officer successfully purchased drugs from a dealer named Eric Duprey. As officers moved in to arrest him and his accomplice, Duprey fled the scene on a motorcycle. The drug dealer drove up onto the narrow sidewalk at 25-30 MPH – aiming straight for multiple officers and the detained accomplice. Sgt. Duran had just 2.5 seconds to react. Instead of reaching for his service weapon and neutralizing the threat with deadly force, **he hurled a nearby cooler in the motorcycle’s path.** The criminal hit the cooler, collided with a tree, and passed away from his injuries. 999 times out of 1,000, the suspect would have been stopped – uninjured – and the officer would be celebrated for using non-lethal force to stop a deadly threat. Instead, the anti-cop radicals in NYC went crazy and Letitia James’ office brought charges against him. Sgt. Duran was convicted of Manslaughter and sentenced to 3-9 years in prison. He has been released on bail pending his appeal. **[Now I hope you can see why I’m asking you to help Sgt. Duran fight back.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** My name is Jason Johnson and I am the president of the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF). For over 30 years, LELDF has successfully defended wrongly accused officers like Sgt. Duran – getting charges dropped, convictions overturned, and even securing presidential pardons. Our track record of success is unmatched. But as a 501(c)3 non-profit organization, we don’t receive taxpayer funding or government grants. Our efforts are powered by patriots like you who donate $35, $50, $100, $250, $500, or even $1,000. Unfortunately, this appeal is shaping up to be the costliest in LELDF’s 32-year history with early estimates reaching $1,000,000. And since Erik’s family – his wife and three young children – have received numerous death threats, that estimate will only increase if paid security is required. **[Can I count on you help fund Sgt. Duran’s appeal and secure his freedom by making a tax-deductible donation of $35, $50, $100, $250, $500, or more today?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** During his 15 years on the force, Erik received 39 commendations and was credited with removing at least 50 illegal firearms from the streets of New York. To say he will have a target on his back in prison is a gross understatement. As a retired police officer and father, I can only imagine the fear of knowing the danger he and his family face. And that he may not be there to protect them. **[So, please – no matter how much or how little you can give today – stand with me and fight for Sgt. Duran’s freedom.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** Your donation will be put to immediate use helping Sgt. Duran and a dozen other officers heading to trial. Thank you in advance!
---
| | | Gratefully,
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Jason C. Johnson President, Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund
---
P.S. During Sgt. Duran’s sentencing, the judge said “Suspects sometimes get away and can be captured later. He [Duprey] could have been caught on a different day.” My friend, tell that to the widow of NYPD Detective Jonathan Diller – whose killer was acquitted of first-degree murder and instead convicted of “aggravated manslaughter” just days after Erik was convicted. In this war against cops, officers do not have time to second-guess their instincts. They must act quickly and decisively to save lives. That’s exactly what Sgt. Erik Duran did with the utmost concern for protecting life. He should never have been charged in the first place, let alone convicted – and [**I pray you’ll help fund his appeal by donating to the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund today.** Thank you!](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
[ **Stand with Erik Duran** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---

clean_body: | | | | | | | | | Fellow American, If this highly decorated NYPD officer had used his service weapon, I probably wouldn’t be sending you this message... ...but because Sgt. Erik Duran chose non-lethal force to stop a fleeing criminal, he’s staring down nine years behind bars. Side-by-side with the violent criminals he helped put away during his exemplary 15-year career in law enforcement. You see, in August 2023, NYPD Sgt. Erik Duran was part of an undercover narcotics “buy-and-bust” operation in the Bronx. An officer successfully purchased drugs from a dealer named Eric Duprey. As officers moved in to arrest him and his accomplice, Duprey fled the scene on a motorcycle. The drug dealer drove up onto the narrow sidewalk at 25-30 MPH – aiming straight for multiple officers and the detained accomplice. Sgt. Duran had just 2.5 seconds to react. Instead of reaching for his service weapon and neutralizing the threat with deadly force, he hurled a nearby cooler in the motorcycle’s path. The criminal hit the cooler, collided with a tree, and passed away from his injuries. 999 times out of 1,000, the suspect would have been stopped – uninjured – and the officer would be celebrated for using non-lethal force to stop a deadly threat. Instead, the anti-cop radicals in NYC went crazy and Letitia James’ office brought charges against him. Sgt. Duran was convicted of Manslaughter and sentenced to 3-9 years in prison. He has been released on bail pending his appeal. My name is Jason Johnson and I am the president of the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF). For over 30 years, LELDF has successfully defended wrongly accused officers like Sgt. Duran – getting charges dropped, convictions overturned, and even securing presidential pardons. Our track record of success is unmatched. But as a 501(c)3 non-profit organization, we don’t receive taxpayer funding or government grants. Our efforts are powered by patriots like you who donate $35, $50, $100, $250, $500, or even $1,000. Unfortunately, this appeal is shaping up to be the costliest in LELDF’s 32-year history with early estimates reaching $1,000,000. And since Erik’s family – his wife and three young children – have received numerous death threats, that estimate will only increase if paid security is required. During his 15 years on the force, Erik received 39 commendations and was credited with removing at least 50 illegal firearms from the streets of New York. To say he will have a target on his back in prison is a gross understatement. As a retired police officer and father, I can only imagine the fear of knowing the danger he and his family face. And that he may not be there to protect them. Your donation will be put to immediate use helping Sgt. Duran and a dozen other officers heading to trial. Thank you in advance! | | | Gratefully, Jason C. Johnson President, Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund P.S. During Sgt. Duran’s sentencing, the judge said “Suspects sometimes get away and can be captured later. He [Duprey] could have been caught on a different day.” My friend, tell that to the widow of NYPD Detective Jonathan Diller – whose killer was acquitted of first-degree murder and instead convicted of “aggravated manslaughter” just days after Erik was convicted. In this war against cops, officers do not have time to second-guess their instincts. They must act quickly and decisively to save lives. That’s exactly what Sgt. Erik Duran did with the utmost concern for protecting life. He should never have been charged in the first place, let alone convicted – and | | | More such officers who sacrifice so much for will face similar fates unless we speak out and stand up for the brave men and women in blue. The next time you see a police officer in your community, please thank them for their service. To read more about our mission or the other Law Enforcement officers we're defending, please visit www.leldf.org. name: Justin J. Pearson
subject: This isn't just about lines on a map. It’s about whether our community gets a voice at all.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Justice Democrats
body:
I wanted you to hear this from me first.
#
Peter, I wanted to provide an update of where things stand right now.
No matter what happens next — no matter whether Tennessee ends up using the old maps or these new, racist maps that seek to _eliminate_ our district’s identity — **I’m still running to represent TN-09.**
Our Movement _fully_ supports the lawsuit to overturn this blatant gerrymander. We’re fighting this in the courts, in the streets, and by organizing our neighbors, because we _need to make it crystal clear_ to MAGA Republicans that we _refuse_ to yield.
**[But we can’t do this work without you, Peter. I hope you’ll join our campaign in our fight to restore our right to fair representation by splitting $10 or anything you can spare right now between our campaign and Justice Democrats.](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260513-jp.RyULUa&refcode=em20260513-37772&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=2&akid=37772%2E1203867%2EcwZXNf)**
**[Chip in $10 now! →](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260513-jp.RyULUa&refcode=em20260513-37772&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=3&akid=37772%2E1203867%2EcwZXNf)**
Let’s be clear about why we’re here. We’re here because the far-right knows they can’t _win_ fair and square.
So they’ve rigged the playing field. They’ve redrawn the board. And they’re trying to choose their voters, instead of letting voters choose their leaders.
They want to disrespect our dignity for the sake of politics. They want to roll back our hard-fought rights. And they want to manipulate our democracy behind closed doors.
_**I won’t stand for it, and I know you won’t either.**_
Whether we run in the “old” or “new” District 9, our vision for the future hasn’t changed. We’re still going to fight against xAI and other polluters for clean water to drink and clean air to breathe. We’re still going to fight to end gun violence that keeps stealing our loved ones. And we’re still going to fight a democracy that belongs to the People — not to lobbyists, special interests, and not to politicians who are terrified of losing power.
That’s why this moment matters so much. Because this isn’t just about lines on a map. It’s about whether our community gets a voice at all.
But keeping our district’s voice alive is going to take resources. **[That’s why I’m asking you to split $10 or more in the next 30 minutes so we can close the gap to $100,000 and keep our momentum going in this critical moment.](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260513-jp.RyULUa&refcode=em20260513-37772&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=4&akid=37772%2E1203867%2EcwZXNf)**
